content.title: [Story]: Agent can mark two items as "related" without implying a hard blocking dependency
content.body:
As the Scrum Master agent, I can mark two backlog items as "related" so that complementary or thematically linked stories remain discoverable on the board without implying one blocks the other.

## Background
The current dependency model supports only `blocked_by`/`blocks` (hard upstream/downstream blocking). Items that share context, operate on the same component, or are complementary stories cannot be linked without incorrectly implying a sequencing constraint. Example: #187 ("pass through non-canonical fields in normalizer") and #216 ("strip canonical fields from normalizer") are two sides of the same component story — invisible to each other on the board.

## Desired Behaviour
`scrum_update_story` accepts a `related_to: StoryRef[]` field. Related items appear in `scrum_get_item_detail` responses and in `scrum_find_items` listings as a `related` array. No ordering, blocking, or sprint-planning semantics are implied.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scrum_update_story` accepts `related_to: [{ id: string }]` to set related items (replaces existing related set, consistent with existing `blocked_by` behaviour)
- [ ] `scrum_get_item_detail` response includes `related: [{ key, title }]` when related items exist
- [ ] `scrum_find_items` listings include `related: [{ key }]` (keys only — no titles, to keep listing payload small)
- [ ] Related links are bidirectional — linking A → B automatically surfaces B in A's related list and A in B's
- [ ] Related links do not affect DoR checks, dependency graph traversal, or sprint risk counts
- [ ] Tool description for `scrum_update_story` documents the `related_to` parameter

content.title: [User Story]: Developer has PlatformVocabularyMap interface + GitHub implementation — all Scrum concepts mapped to/from GitHub primitives
content.body:
### User Story

As a **developer adding a new backend integration**, I have **a `PlatformVocabularyMap` interface with a working GitHub implementation**, so that **I understand how Scrum concepts translate to platform primitives — and can replicate the pattern for my backend**.

### Problem

Without a formal vocabulary mapping, each backend implements Scrum concept encoding/decoding ad-hoc. There's no contract for how `type`, `status`, `sprint`, `priority`, `story_points`, `epic`, `blocked_by`, and `labels` map between Scrum semantics and platform primitives.

### Solution

Implement `PlatformVocabularyMap` interface and GitHub concrete implementation:
- For each Scrum concept: `support: CapabilityStatus`, `encode(ScrumValue) → PlatformValue`, `decode(PlatformValue) → ScrumValue`, `constraint?: string`
- `isSpecialLabel(platformLabel) → boolean` — returns true if label encodes Scrum metadata
- `extractUserLabels(allPlatformLabels) → string[]` — strips special labels, returns user-facing ones
- GitHub implementation maps type/status/sprint/priority/story_points/epic/blocked_by through GitHub Projects V2 custom fields

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PlatformVocabularyMap` interface defined with encode/decode/constraint per Scrum concept
- [ ] GitHub implementation decodes all concepts from project V2 field values correctly
- [ ] `isSpecialLabel` correctly identifies Scrum metadata labels vs. user labels
- [ ] `extractUserLabels` strips special labels, returns only user-facing ones
- [ ] Normalizer uses vocabulary map for all field decode calls
- [ ] Existing tests pass with the vocabulary map integrated

### Dependencies
- [ ] AbstractAssembler implemented
- [ ] CapabilityStatus enum exists

content.title: [User Story]: Agent receives factual capability statements — NATIVE/EMULATED/UNAVAILABLE for every operation
content.body:
### User Story

As an **agent user**, I want to receive **factual capability statements from the backend** (NATIVE, EMULATED, or UNAVAILABLE for every operation), so that **I know what operations are possible and what limitations apply — without silent degradation**.

### Problem

The current `PlatformCapabilities` uses boolean flags (`canCreateSprints: boolean`). Booleans can't express that an operation works but with emulation constraints. The agent cannot distinguish between "fully supported," "works with limitations," and "impossible."

### Solution

Replace boolean flags with a three-value `CapabilityStatus` enum:
- `NATIVE` — operation maps directly to a platform API call; full fidelity
- `EMULATED` — supported by encoding scrum semantics onto available primitives; constraints apply
- `UNAVAILABLE` — cannot be expressed on this platform

Every field in `PlatformCapabilities` becomes `CapabilityStatus`. Operations with `EMULATED` status must document their emulation contract. `UNAVAILABLE` operations throw `CapabilityUnavailableError` with a `recoverySuggestion`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CapabilityStatus` enum replaces booleans in `PlatformCapabilities`
- [ ] `getCapabilities()` returns a `CapabilityMap` derived from the statuses
- [ ] Updating a capability status updates the map automatically — no separate sync needed
- [ ] `EMULATED` operations proceed with a warning appended to `warnings[]`
- [ ] `UNAVAILABLE` operations throw `CapabilityUnavailableError` with `recoverySuggestion`
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new tests cover all three statuses

### Dependencies
None — independent. Can be done in parallel with other streams.

content.title: [Bug]: scrum_find_items custom_fields duplicates top-level fields as JSON-stringified GitHub API noise — 40–50% per-item payload waste
content.body:
## Problem

`scrum_find_items` listing responses include a `custom_fields` block where each value is a JSON-serialized string containing raw GitHub ProjectV2 API shapes. The content duplicates fields already present as structured top-level properties on every listing item — `status`, `priority`, `type`, `story_points`, `sprint`, `labels`, `assignees`, `epic` — and wraps them in GitHub-internal metadata that has no agent utility: `__typename`, `color`, `optionId`, and `nameWithOwner`.

**Example — `status` appears twice per item:**

Top level (useful): `"status": "Done"`

In custom_fields (noise):
```
"Status": "{\"__typename\":\"ProjectV2ItemFieldSingleSelectValue\",\"name\":\"Done\",\"color\":\"GREEN\",\"optionId\":\"4ad38d58\"}"
```

`enrichListingCustomFields()` in `result-normalizer.ts` serializes all GitHub field value nodes, including those already mapped to canonical top-level fields.

## Impact

At ~600 chars average overhead per item, a 50-item `scrum_find_items` response carries ~30KB of wasted context — a direct token cost on every agent session. Live measurement during grooming session 2026-06-03 estimated 40–50% of per-item payload is redundant.

`custom_fields` exists as a passthrough for genuinely non-canonical fields only (see companion issue #187). The canonical field set belongs at the top level, not here.

## Affected file

`src/adapters/github/internal/result-normalizer.ts` — `enrichListingCustomFields()`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `custom_fields` contains no keys from the canonical field set (Title, Status, Type, Priority, Story Points, Sprint, Assignees, Labels, Milestone, Repository)
- [ ] `color`, `optionId`, and nested `__typename` are excluded from serialized field values
- [ ] Root-level item `__typename` (e.g. `"Issue"`, `"PullRequest"`) is retained as it signals item kind
- [ ] Non-canonical project fields still surface in `custom_fields`
- [ ] Average per-item response size measurably reduced
- [ ] Existing canonical field values on items are unaffected (sourced from top-level mapping, not custom_fields)

content.title: [Story]: Agent can request a minimal listing projection from scrum_find_items for bulk-scan use cases
content.body:
As the Scrum Master agent, I can call `scrum_find_items` with a `projection: "minimal"` parameter so that bulk-scan operations (duplicate checks, grooming prep, board summaries) return only essential fields — eliminating context-window overflow on large boards.

## Background
The playbook-required duplicate scan calls `scrum_find_items(scope: "backlog")`. With a moderately sized backlog (~50 items), the full response (~40–80KB) exceeds the agent's token limit. The agent must fall back to targeted text searches, which are less reliable for semantic deduplication. A minimal projection mode solves this structurally.

## Minimal Projection Fields
`key`, `title`, `type`, `status`, `epic.name` only. All other fields omitted: `story_points`, `assignees`, `labels`, `sprint`, `blocked_by`, `blocks`, `custom_fields`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scrum_find_items({ projection: "minimal" })` returns items with only: `ref.key`, `title`, `type`, `status`, `epic.name`
- [ ] All other fields are absent from minimal projection responses
- [ ] Full projection (all fields) remains the default when `projection` is omitted
- [ ] A 100-item backlog fits within a single response using minimal projection
- [ ] `scope`, `statuses`, `types`, `search`, `epic_id`, and other filters work correctly with `projection: "minimal"`
- [ ] Tool description updated to document the `projection` parameter

content.title: Impediment: Epic CRUD operations are incomplete
content.body:
## Impediment: Epic CRUD operations are incomplete — no create, no close

### What's Missing

The MCP tool surface offers **no ability to create or close epics (milestones)**. Only read (list/search) and assign-to-story operations exist.

### Layer-by-Layer Gap Analysis

**GraphQL (`operations.graphql`):**
- `ListMilestones` query exists (line 492)
- `SetMilestone` mutation exists (line 832) — assigns an existing milestone to an issue
- No `CreateMilestone` mutation
- No `CloseMilestone` mutation
- No `UpdateMilestone` mutation

**Port interface (`src/scrum/ports.ts`):**
- `EpicPort` (line 292) has only `getEpics()` — single read method
- `ProjectWriter` (line 381) has no epic create/close/update methods
- No `CreateStoryInput`-equivalent for epics (`CreateEpicInput`)

**Adapter (`src/adapters/github/backend.ts`):**
- `getEpics()` delegates to `EpicService` — works for reads
- No `createEpic()` override — `AbstractProjectBackend` doesn't even declare it
- No `closeEpic()` override — same

**Capabilities (`src/adapters/capabilities.ts`):**
- `PlatformCapabilities` has no flag for epic CRUD support (only `auditLogBurndown`, `nativeSprints`, `dependencies`, `fileReader`, `stableItemKeys`)

### Impact

1. Agent must instruct users to create milestones manually in the GitHub UI, then wait for the user to paste the milestone ID back
2. Agent cannot create epics as part of sprint planning
3. Closing a completed epic requires manual GitHub action
4. The just-created "Adapter Layer Assembly Pattern" epic for this project had to be created by the user outside the tool

### Recommended Fix

1. Add `CreateMilestone` and `CloseMilestone` mutations to `operations.graphql`
2. Add `createEpic(input)` and `closeEpic(ref)` to `ProjectWriter` and `EpicPort` ports
3. Implement in `GitHubProjectBackend` via a new method or `EpicService` extension
4. Add MCP tools: `scrum_create_epic(title, description?)` and `scrum_close_epic(ref)`

### Escalation

Day 1 of this impediment. Escalation threshold: Day 2 if no action is taken.

---

## Sub-Impediment: New epics don't appear in `scrum_orient` until they have items in the active sprint

### Root Cause

In `EpicService.getEpics()` (line 50-81), when `sprintIterationId` is `"current"`, the function:
1. Fetches all milestones
2. Fetches items in the active sprint
3. Collects epic IDs that have ≥1 item in the sprint
4. **Filters out milestones NOT in that set**

A newly created milestone with zero items is invisible in `scrum_orient`.

### Impact

- The "Adapter Layer Assembly Pattern" epic doesn't show up in `scrum_orient`'s `epics.active[]` list
- The agent can't verify the epic exists after creation
- Affects any workflow where an epic is created then needs immediate interaction

### Recommended Fix

In `EpicService.getEpics()`: when `sprintIterationId` is `"current"`, return **all open milestones** regardless of sprint item count. The sprint-based filtering should only apply when a specific sprint is requested (not `"current"`). Alternatively, `orientUseCase` in `orient.ts` should call `getEpics(null)` (all milestones) and apply its own `status !== "done"` filter, instead of passing `"current"`.

content.title: [Spike]: Audit adapter-layer query formation pipeline — trace use case requests to GraphQL payloads and identify urgent query-level optimization opportunities
content.body:
## Context

The adapter layer translates use case requests (`ResolvedItemFilter` and other
port inputs) into GitHub GraphQL operations. This translation path — from port
contract through query assembly to wire payload — is currently implicit,
inconsistent across assembler branches, and suspected to be over-fetching
significantly relative to what each use case actually needs.

This spike audits the query formation pipeline within the adapter layer only.
It produces a concrete payload analysis for each assembler branch and identifies
which query-level optimizations are viable without touching the use case layer
or framework layer. No implementation changes.

This spike is downstream of #190 (full call graph audit) but can run in
parallel — #190 maps the system-wide call structure; this spike goes deeper
into how each individual query is formed and what it fetches.

## Scope constraint

All findings and optimization candidates must be achievable within
`src/adapters/github/` only. Changes to port interfaces (`src/scrum/ports.ts`),
use case functions (`src/scrum/`), or tool handlers (`src/tools/`) are out of
scope.

## Time-box

1–2 focused investigation sessions. Includes live API validation for question 3.

## Questions to Answer

1. **How does a use case request traverse the adapter layer to become a
   GitHub GraphQL request?**
   Trace the full path: `ResolvedItemFilter` → `classifyFilter()` →
   `FilterProfile` → assembler → `PlatformRequest` → `ExecutionEngine` →
   `gh.graphql()`. Document each transformation step and what information
   is preserved, added, or discarded at each boundary.

2. **For each assembler branch (`direct_lookup`, `search_api`,
   `project_items`, `mixed`): what does the query actually fetch vs.
   what does the use case need?**
   For each branch: identify the GraphQL operation name, the fragments
   included, and every field selected. Then cross-reference against what
   the calling use case actually reads from the response. Document the
   gap — fields fetched but never consumed.

3. **What GitHub API calls can we use for better server-side filtering
   in the context of our application?**
   Survey the full range of available GitHub API capabilities — GraphQL
   and REST — that could push filtering work to the server rather than
   the client. For each candidate (e.g. `fieldValueFilters` on the
   `projectV2.items()` connection, Search API query parameters, issue
   timeline filters, etc.): validate against the live API, document the
   exact query or endpoint, confirm whether it handles our field types
   (iteration, single-select, number), and note any pagination or
   result-count differences compared to the current client-side approach.
   The goal is a complete picture of what GitHub will actually let us
   filter server-side, not an assumption based on documentation alone.

4. **For each assembler branch, what is the minimum viable query — the
   smallest fragment set that satisfies the use case's actual data
   requirements?**
   Given the gap found in question 2 and the server-side filtering
   capabilities confirmed in question 3, what would the lean query look
   like? Which fragment fields can be removed or made conditional without
   breaking any downstream consumer?

5. **Which optimization changes are safe to make within the adapter layer
   alone, and what is the urgency ordering?**
   Classify each candidate by: (a) adapter-layer-only vs. requires port
   change, (b) estimated payload reduction, (c) implementation complexity.
   Urgency = payload reduction × frequency of the call path.

## Output

Findings documented as a comment on this issue before closing.

---

### Diagram — Query formation pipeline (PlantUML sequence)

One sequence diagram tracing the full formation path from `ResolvedItemFilter`
entry to `gh.graphql()` call, for the `project_items` branch (the most
complex). Show each transformation boundary as a lifeline, the data object
passed at each step, and where fragment selection occurs.

```plantuml
@startuml
' sequence diagram
@enduml
```

---

### Payload analysis table

One row per assembler branch. Columns:

| Branch | Operation | Fragments used | Field count fetched | Field count consumed | Excess % | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| direct_lookup | | | | | | |
| search_api | | | | | | |
| project_items | | | | | | |
| mixed | | | | | | |

---

### Server-side filtering capabilities

For each GitHub API capability validated in question 3: the mechanism
(GraphQL field, REST endpoint, or query parameter), the exact fragment or
request tested, which of our filter dimensions it supports (sprint/iteration,
status, type, assignee, labels, text), and the live API result. Conclude with
a ranked summary of which capabilities are viable for immediate use in our
assembler branches.

---

### Optimization candidates

| Candidate | Change description | Layer-safe? | Est. payload reduction | Complexity | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | Adapter-only / Requires port change | | Low / Med / High | |

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Query formation path traced and documented for all four assembler branches
- [ ] Payload analysis table completed — fetched vs. consumed fields for each branch
- [ ] Server-side filtering capabilities surveyed and validated against the live API;
      all viable mechanisms documented with evidence
- [ ] Minimum viable query documented for each branch where a gap exists
- [ ] Optimization candidates classified by layer-safety and urgency
- [ ] A follow-on story or tech debt item created for each optimization
      candidate that is adapter-layer-safe and high-urgency, before this
      spike closes
- [ ] Findings comment posted before closing this issue

content.title: [Spike]: Audit tool surface → GitHub API call graph — map every MCP tool invocation to its full wire-level call sequence
content.body:
## Context

Every MCP tool invocation triggers one or more GitHub API calls, but the
relationship between the tool surface and the underlying wire-level calls is
undocumented and not obvious from the architecture. Internal services make
`gh.graphql()` calls directly, independently, and sometimes redundantly — with
no shared understanding of what fires, in what order, or why.

Before any adapter optimization work can be scoped or prioritized, we need a
complete, accurate map of what actually happens at the network layer for every
tool invocation — from tool handler entry point to the last byte on the wire.
This is a read-only audit. No implementation changes.

The output will directly determine the scope, priority, and content of all
downstream adapter tickets including the query optimization and assembler
design work.

## Time-box

1–2 focused investigation sessions. Trace source code only — no live API
profiling required.

## Questions to Answer

For each MCP tool (`scrum_orient`, `scrum_find_items`, `scrum_get_item_detail`,
`scrum_get_board_health`, `scrum_get_analytics`, `scrum_create_story`,
`scrum_update_story`, `scrum_set_field`, `scrum_log_impediment`,
`scrum_update_impediment`, `scrum_add_vocabulary`):

1. **What is the full API call sequence?**
   Trace from the tool handler through the use case layer, backend facade,
   and into each internal service. Document every `gh.graphql()` and
   `gh.request()` call that fires, in order, with the operation name.

2. **What is the dependency structure between those calls?**
   Which calls are inherently sequential (the response of call N is required
   to form call N+1), and which are structurally independent (they could fire
   in parallel but currently don't)?

3. **Which calls are unconditional vs. conditionally fired?**
   Does the call fire on every invocation, or is it gated on input shape,
   ref type, or config state?

4. **Where does the system make the same underlying API call more than once —
   within a single tool invocation or across tools?**
   Identify duplicated calls within one invocation (e.g. bootstrap firing at
   factory init and again inside orient) and calls whose results are
   recomputed from scratch across tools that could share a cached result.

5. **Which tool invocations bypass the structured assembler pipeline and make
   raw unmediated `gh.graphql()` calls directly from service classes?**

6. **What is the minimum theoretically-achievable call count per tool, given
   GitHub's API constraints?**
   If all parallelizable calls were parallelized and all redundant calls
   eliminated, what is the floor?

## Output

All findings documented as a comment on this issue before closing, in the
following format.

---

scope; no internal detail.

Rel(mcp, gh, "graphql(), rest()", "HTTPS")

@enduml

---

content.title: Have `ItemDetailResult` extend `PartialResult` for per-field warning metadata
content.body:
## Problem statement

`ItemDetailResult` has nullable fields (`comments`, `linked_artifacts`) that signal partial completion, but the warnings explaining why those fields are null live on the outer `UseCaseResult.warnings`, not inside the result itself. A consumer holding only an `ItemDetailResult` can't know why data is missing.

[`StoryDetail`](src/scrum/ports.ts:180-184) is already marked deprecated — "Use ItemDetailResult from ../domain/types.ts instead. ItemDetailResult is a superset - it adds acceptance_criteria. StoryDetail will be removed in P2."

## Root cause

`ItemDetailResult` was designed without extending `PartialResult`, so per-field warning metadata is lost when the result is passed to consumers who don't have access to the outer `UseCaseResult`.

## Affected architectural layer

- Domain layer (src/domain/)
- Use-case layer (src/scrum/)

## Risk if deferred

Every consumer of `ItemDetailResult` that needs to explain missing data must also hold the outer `UseCaseResult` — a hidden coupling. This blocks the `StoryDetail` → `ItemDetailResult` migration (P2) and makes error messages to end-users incomplete.

## Proposed approach

1. Add `extends PartialResult` to [`ItemDetailResult`](src/domain/types.ts:577-582)
2. Update [`getStoryUseCase`](src/scrum/get-story.ts) to populate `warnings` inside the `ItemDetailResult` alongside the outer `UseCaseResult`
3. Verify all consumers can access inner warnings

## Done criteria

- [ ] `ItemDetailResult` extends `PartialResult` and inherits the `warnings` field
- [ ] `getStoryUseCase` populates `warnings` inside `ItemDetailResult` with per-field explanations
- [ ] All existing consumers still compile and function correctly
- [ ] A consumer holding just an `ItemDetailResult` can determine why `comments` or `linked_artifacts` is null

## Story Point Estimate

2

## Additional context / related issues

Discovered during implementation of ticket #125 (Move `PartialFailureResult`). Tied to the deprecated `StoryDetail` → `ItemDetailResult` migration.

content.title: [Bug]: scrum_find_items serializes two structurally misleading empty fields — dependency_map: null and sprint.ref.id: ""
content.body:
## Problem

Every `scrum_find_items` response contains two structurally misleading empty fields that waste agent context and can silently mislead parsers.

**1. `dependency_map: null` serialized when not requested**

When `include_dependencies` is false (the default for all normal queries), the response root still contains `"dependency_map": null`. A null key at the root serializes to nothing useful and should be omitted. The field has meaning only when `include_dependencies: true` is explicitly passed.

**2. `sprint.ref.id: ""` for items with no sprint assignment**

Items not assigned to a sprint carry:
```json
"sprint": { "name": null, "ref": { "id": "" } }
```
An empty string ID is indistinguishable from a valid iteration ID to any parser that does not special-case it. The `epic` field handles the equivalent case correctly — returning `null` for unassigned items. Sprint should be consistent.

`EMPTY_SPRINT_REF` is documented as a known gap in `listing-mappers.ts`.

## Impact

Minor per-call token waste that compounds across every query. The empty `sprint.ref.id` is a correctness issue — silent misrepresentation of "no sprint" as a value that resembles a valid ID.

## Affected files

- `src/scrum/listing-mappers.ts` — `EMPTY_SPRINT_REF` constant, `toItemListing()`
- Response serialization — `dependency_map` omission

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scrum_find_items` response without `include_dependencies: true` contains no `dependency_map` key
- [ ] `scrum_find_items` response with `include_dependencies: true` still contains `dependency_map` with full graph data
- [ ] Unassigned sprint renders as `sprint: null`, not `{ name: null, ref: { id: "" } }`
- [ ] No existing consumers of `sprint.ref.id` break (all call sites audited before merging)
- [ ] Response size reduced for the common no-dependency case

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Replace readiness.by_type in scrum_get_board_health with flat active-item risk counts
content.body:
## Current State
`scrum_get_board_health` computes a `readiness.by_type` object applying DoR rules (AC check, estimation check, type check) server-side and returns ready/not-ready counts across 6 item types. When the sprint has no active items (e.g. next sprint), this produces 18 zero-valued fields. DoR interpretation belongs to the agent, not the server.

## Problems
1. When the sprint has no active items, 18 zero-valued fields are returned — pure noise
2. Server deciding "this item is not ready" conflicts with the agent's responsibility to apply DoR rules from `scrum_orient` vocabulary
3. `overall_pct` presents a conclusion rather than facts the agent can reason from

## Cost of Deferral
Every board health call carries agent-layer reasoning in the server, increasing tool coupling and making the health endpoint harder to evolve.

## Desired State
Replace `readiness` with a flat `active_items` object:
```json
{
  "active_items": {
    "total": 4,
    "unestimated": 1,
    "no_type": 0,
    "no_ac": 0,
    "no_assignee": 1,
    "blocked": 0
  }
}
```
Return `"active_items": null` when the sprint has no active items.

**DoD note:** SKILL.md agent rules referencing `readiness.by_type` or `overall_pct` must be updated to use `active_items` counts and apply DoR rules from `scrum_orient` vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scrum_get_board_health` response no longer contains `readiness` or `overall_pct` fields
- [ ] Response contains `active_items` with fields: `total`, `unestimated`, `no_type`, `no_ac`, `no_assignee`, `blocked`
- [ ] `active_items` counts exclude Done-status items
- [ ] When no active items exist for the sprint scope, `active_items` is `null`
- [ ] SKILL.md updated: references to `readiness.by_type` or `overall_pct` replaced with `active_items` reasoning pattern
- [ ] Agent using `active_items.unestimated > 0` correctly identifies unestimated work without server interpretation

content.title: [Bug]: scope:"sprint" returns items from past sprints — checks sprint existence, not current sprint identity
content.body:
**Observed behaviour:** Calling `scrum_find_items` with `scope: "sprint"` combined with a type filter (e.g. `types: ["bug"]`) returns items from completed past sprints (e.g. Sprint 2 Done bugs) alongside current sprint items.

**Expected behaviour:** `scope: "sprint"` returns only items assigned to the currently active sprint.

**Root cause:** In `item-filter.ts`, the scope check is:
```ts
if (filter.scope === "sprint" && story.sprint === null) return false;
```
`story.sprint` stores the sprint name string (e.g. `"Sprint 2"`), which is non-null for any item that has ever been sprint-assigned. The predicate excludes only sprint-less items, not items from past sprints.

**Fix:** Compare `story.sprint` against the active sprint name from `config.live.iterations.active?.name`:
```ts
const activeSprintName = config.live.iterations.active?.name ?? null;
if (filter.scope === "sprint" && story.sprint !== activeSprintName) return false;
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scrum_find_items({ scope: "sprint" })` returns only items assigned to the currently active sprint
- [ ] Items from completed sprints are excluded from `scope: "sprint"` results
- [ ] `scope: "backlog"` continues to exclude items with any sprint assignment
- [ ] Combining `scope: "sprint"` with `types` or `statuses` filters returns only active-sprint items of the specified type/status
- [ ] When no active sprint exists, `scope: "sprint"` returns an empty result

content.body:
**Observed behaviour:** Calling `scrum_find_items` with a `keys` argument (e.g. `keys: ["202"]`) returns a GraphQL error:

- [ ] Passing an invalid key (e.g. `keys: ["99999"]`) returns an empty items array, not an error

content.title: [Bug]: scrum_update_story rejects epic field — EpicRefSchema.or(z.null()) union causes object-to-string serialization failure
content.body:
**Observed behaviour:** Calling `scrum_update_story` with `epic: { id: "..." }` returns:
> Invalid input: expected object, received string (path: epic)

**Expected behaviour:** The epic field is accepted and the story's milestone is updated.

**Root cause:** In `schemas/scrum.ts`, `UpdateStorySchema` defines:
```ts
epic: EpicRefSchema.or(z.null()).optional()
```
Zod's `.or(z.null())` creates a `ZodUnion`. When the MCP SDK serializes this via `.shape` into JSON Schema, the union produces an `anyOf: [object, null]` structure. The MCP harness receives the incoming `{ id: string }` value and coerces it to a string when validating against the union, causing the type error.

`scrum_create_story` uses `EpicRefSchema.optional()` (no union) — this works correctly.

**Fix:**
```ts
// Before
epic: EpicRefSchema.or(z.null()).optional()

// After
epic: EpicRefSchema.nullable().optional()
```
Zod's `.nullable()` generates a cleaner JSON Schema representation that the MCP SDK handles without the coercion issue.

**Workaround until fixed:** Epic reassignment must be done manually on the GitHub project board.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scrum_update_story({ ref: { id: "..." }, epic: { id: "..." } })` succeeds and updates the story's milestone
- [ ] `scrum_update_story({ ref: { id: "..." }, epic: null })` succeeds and detaches the story from its epic
- [ ] `scrum_update_story` with `epic` omitted leaves the existing epic unchanged
- [ ] `scrum_create_story` epic behaviour is unaffected
- [ ] Unit test covering the nullable epic path in UpdateStorySchema

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Remove silent config fallback — make --config mandatory
content.body:
### Problem

The server silently falls back to `.github/scrum/config.yml` when no `--config` flag or `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` env var is provided. When that default path doesn't exist, the server starts in "degraded mode" with stub tools — every tool call returns `"Config not found"` instead of crashing at startup with a clear error.

This masks a genuine configuration error. A developer who starts from the wrong directory or without knowing the flag sees a running process that does nothing useful.

### Diagnosis

**Layer 1 — Server** (`src/server.ts:117-121`): `_configLocation: ContentLocation | undefined` — becomes `undefined` when no config source is provided. The type itself lies (T4 — lying function signature cascade).

**Layer 2 — Adapter** (`src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:360-363`): `params.configLocation ?? { kind: "file", path: resolve(Deno.cwd(), ".github/scrum/config.yml") }` — a hidden default path.

**Cascade — ConfigReloader** (`src/adapters/github/internal/config-reloader.ts:19`): calls `loadConfig({ github: this.github })` without `configLocation` — will silently break if the `??` fallback is removed without updating this site.

### Impact if not fixed

- **Bad UX:** Server starts without error but every tool fails silently
- **Hidden coupling:** The adapter embeds a default path that only works when CWD is the project root
- **Type debt:** `ContentLocation | undefined` propagates through 5 function/interface signatures where the value is actually always required

### Implementation — 11 sites, 6 files

1. `src/server.ts:114-121` — Add `if (!_rawConfigPath) { console.error(); Deno.exit(1); }`
2. `src/server.ts:78-87` — Help text: remove "(default: .github/scrum/config.yml)", add "(required)"
3. `src/server.ts:245-247` — `createMcpServer(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
4. `src/server.ts:262-277` — Simplify error branches (remove dead `else if` / `else`)
5. `src/server.ts:339-341` — `runStdio(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
6. `src/server.ts:366` — `runHttp(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
7. `src/adapters/factory.ts:18-23` — `AdapterStartupOptions.configLocation` required
8. `src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:72-77` — `ConfigParams.configLocation` required
9. `src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:360-363` — Remove `??` fallback
10. `src/adapters/github/internal/config-reloader.ts:12-19` — Add `configLocation` param
11. `src/adapters/github/factory.ts:119` — Pass `configLocation` to `ConfigReloader`

### What stays

- `registerStubTools()` — still needed for `AUTH_FAILED` degraded mode
- `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` — still supported (now mandatory)
- The `try/catch` around `createBackend` — needed for other adapter errors

Full plan: `plans/remove-config-fallback.md`

- [ ] Server exits with code 1 and clear message when no `--config` or `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` set
- [ ] All `ContentLocation | undefined` signatures updated to `ContentLocation` (no lying optionality)

content.title: [Bug]: Server crashes when --config is a remote GitHub blob URL
content.body:
### Problem

Using a GitHub blob URL (`https://github.com/owner/repo/blob/branch/path`) as the `--config` argument causes the tool server to crash (process exit) instead of entering degraded mode with a friendly error.

The server advertises support for remote URLs in `--help`, but GitHub blob URLs return HTML, not raw YAML content.

### Reproduction

1. Start the server with:
   ```
   node dist/server.mjs --config https://github.com/owner/repo/blob/main/.github/scrum/config.yml
   ```
2. The server fetches the URL, receives an HTML page (content-type: text/html), and attempts to parse it as YAML.
3. The YAML parser fails with: `end of the stream or a document separator is expected`
4. The error propagates out as an unhandled exception, killing the process.

### Expected Behavior

When `--config` points to an unreachable, unparseable, or wrong-format URL:

- The server should enter **degraded mode** with stub tools that return a clear error message.
- The error message should indicate that the URL returned HTML instead of YAML, and suggest using `raw.githubusercontent.com` URLs instead.

### Actual Behavior

The `loadScrumConfig()` call at `src/server.ts:273` is **outside** the `try/catch` block that handles backend initialization errors. When it throws, the error propagates to `runStdio()`'s catch, which calls `emitJsonRpcError()` + `Deno.exit(1)`. The MCP client sees the process exit unexpectedly and reports a crash.

### Diagnosis

- `fetch-location.ts`: Successfully fetches the URL — gets a 200 OK response with `content-type: text/html`.
- `config-boot.ts`: Attempts YAML parse on HTML → parse failure → throws.
- `server.ts:273`: The thrown error is not caught by the `try/catch` at line 276 — it only wraps `createBackend()`, not `loadScrumConfig()`.
- `emitJsonRpcError()` writes an unsolicited JSON-RPC error response to stdout (the MCP client hasn't sent `initialize` yet), then `Deno.exit(1)` terminates the process.

### Environment

- Bundle: Node.js (dist/server.mjs)
- URL format: `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/blob/{branch}/{path}` (returns HTML)
- Required format: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/{repo}/{branch}/{path}` (returns raw YAML)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Starting the server with a GitHub blob `--config` URL enters degraded mode with stub tools instead of crashing
- [ ] The error message includes a hint about using `raw.githubusercontent.com` URLs
- [ ] Starting the server with a valid `raw.githubusercontent.com` config URL works correctly
- [ ] All existing local path and inline config modes continue to work

## Debt Description

### Part A — Dead functions (from #109)

Two functions in [`src/scrum/sprint-math.ts`](src/scrum/sprint-math.ts) have **zero importers**:

- `computeSprintTotals` (line 53) — never called by any use case
- `groupStoriesByStatus` (line 90) — never called by any use case

### Part B — Duplicated sprint date math (from #114)

Sprint date computation is duplicated in **three places** with slightly different implementations:

1. [`src/scrum/sprint-math.ts:26-28`](src/scrum/sprint-math.ts:26) — `buildSprintMeta()`: Uses local-time `setDate`/`setHours`

- Timezone-related bugs may surface unpredictably
- Three implementations to maintain — any fix must be applied in three places

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Update agent behavioral rules for the redesigned tool surface
content.body:
## Problem statement

The agent rules in `.roo/` still reference the old tool surface: `scrum_get_sprint`, `scrum_get_backlog`, `scrum_get_story`, `scrum_get_burndown`, `scrum_get_history`, and `scrum_get_template`. The session start protocol unconditionally calls `scrum_get_backlog` regardless of task type, and the rules contain no guidance on direct item lookup, dependency graph usage, or task-driven health loading.

## Root cause

The rules were written against the original tool surface and have not been updated to reflect the redesign. Behavioral guidance is encoded in rules files, not inferred from tool descriptions alone.

## Affected architectural layer

Agent mode (`.roo/`)

## Risk if deferred

Even with the new tools shipped, the agent will fall back to old patterns — full board dumps for single-ticket requests, unconditional health loads on every session, no use of the dependency graph opt-in — defeating the performance and clarity goals of the entire epic.

## Proposed approach

### 1. Update session start protocol
`scrum_orient` → gap check → classify and route. Remove unconditional `scrum_get_backlog` call.

Encode task-driven health-loading table:

| Session type | Load board health? |
|---|---|
| Planning / refinement / retrospective / ambiguous | Yes → `scrum_get_board_health` |
| Single item lookup or targeted write on named item | No |

### 2. Encode sprint risk stance from orient (pre-computed)

`scrum_orient` returns `platform_state.iterations.active.riskStance` as a pre-computed field.
**Do not recompute it from `time_elapsed_pct` alone.**

The server computes it as `time_elapsed_pct / work_pct` ratio:
- `normal` — time ≤ 110% of work completed
- `monitor` — time between 110–130% of work completed
- `elevated` — time ≥ 130% of work completed, or time > 0 with no work done

Agent rule: read `riskStance` from orient; act on `normal` / `monitor` / `elevated` directly.

### 3. Encode direct lookup pattern

- **Single item full detail** (body, comments, AC, linked PRs): `scrum_get_item_detail(ref: { number: N })`
- **Multi-item listing** by issue numbers: `scrum_find_items(keys: ["42", "123"])` — keys are **numeric string arrays**
- Never dump the full board to resolve a human-readable reference.

### 4. Encode `scope` vs `sprint_ref` distinction for `scrum_find_items`

Two overlapping sprint filters with different semantics:
- `scope: "sprint"` — returns items whose sprint = the current active sprint (platform's `state.iterations.active`)
- `sprint_ref: "<name>"` — filters by a specific named sprint (any sprint, including completed)

Use `scope: "sprint"` for "what's in the current sprint"; use `sprint_ref` for retrospective or cross-sprint queries.

### 5. Encode impediment lookup pattern

`scrum_get_board_health` returns `impediments: { open_count, orphan_count }` — **counts only, no refs**.
To get actual impediment listings or refs: `scrum_find_items(types: ["impediment"])`.

Replace current rule `scrum_get_backlog labels:["impediment"]` with:
- Health check → `scrum_get_board_health` (counts)
- Logging impediments / linking to items → `scrum_find_items(types: ["impediment"])` (listings with refs)

### 6. Encode template resource access with guard

`scrum_get_template` is removed. Templates are now MCP resources at `scrum://template/{type}`.

Guard required: `templateResourceUseCase` throws if the type is not declared in `typeTemplatePaths`.
Before accessing a template resource, check `platform_state.template_uris` from `scrum_orient`.
Only access `scrum://template/{type}` for types present in that map.

### 7. Encode dependency graph decision table

Fetch-or-skip signals from unresolved `DependencyNode` entries (`resolved: false` in the dependency map returned by `scrum_find_items(include_dependencies: true)`).

### 8. Remove all references to removed tools

Remove: `scrum_get_sprint`, `scrum_get_backlog`, `scrum_get_burndown`, `scrum_get_history`, `scrum_get_template`, `scrum_get_story`.

### 9. Fix schema docstring bugs in `src/schemas/scrum.ts` (additional scope)

Three incorrect docstrings discovered during implementation audit — these are agent-visible via JSON Schema and cause incorrect behavior independent of the rules update:

- **`SprintRefSchema` description**: references `scrum_get_sprint` (removed). Update to reference `scrum_find_items`.
- **`UpdateStorySchema.body` describe**: says `"Call scrum_get_story first"`. Update to `scrum_get_item_detail`.
- **`UpdateImpedimentSchema.ref.id` describe**: says `"scrum_get_board_health.impediments[].ref.id"` — but `BacklogHealth.impediments` only has `{ open_count, orphan_count }`, no `.ref.id`. Update to `"scrum_find_items(types: ['impediment']).items[].ref.id"`.

## Done criteria

- [ ] No reference to `scrum_get_sprint`, `scrum_get_backlog`, `scrum_get_burndown`, `scrum_get_history`, `scrum_get_template`, or `scrum_get_story` in `.roo/`
- [ ] Session start protocol updated with task-driven health-loading table
- [ ] `riskStance` stance table encodes pre-computed field from orient (not a `time_elapsed_pct` threshold table)
- [ ] Direct lookup pattern encoded: `scrum_get_item_detail` for single item; `scrum_find_items(keys: [...])` for multi-item listings
- [ ] `scope` vs `sprint_ref` distinction encoded in rules
- [ ] Impediment lookup pattern encoded: health counts via `scrum_get_board_health`; listings/refs via `scrum_find_items(types: ["impediment"])`
- [ ] Template resource guard encoded: check `platform_state.template_uris` before accessing `scrum://template/{type}`
- [ ] Dependency graph pattern encoded
- [ ] All new tool names (`scrum_find_items`, `scrum_get_item_detail`, `scrum_get_board_health`, `scrum_get_analytics`) referenced correctly
- [ ] Schema docstring bugs fixed in `src/schemas/scrum.ts` (3 items listed above)

As a developer configuring the MCP server, I want to declare item-type display names and template file paths together under a single `type_mapping` key in `config.yml`, and have the server resolve template files from the local workspace before falling back to the remote GitHub API, so that new item types can be added without code changes and templates are immediately available during local development without a commit-push cycle.

content.title: [Bug]: Board item comments land on wrong GitHub issue when project spans multiple repositories
content.body:
## Expected behaviour

When `scrum_update_story` posts a comment on a project board item, the comment appears on the GitHub issue that the board item represents — matching the board item's displayed title and content.

## Actual behaviour

The comment is posted to the underlying GitHub issue that the board item is *linked* to, which may belong to a different repository on the same project board. If the board item's link points to a cross-repo issue, the comment silently lands there instead.

**Observed instance:** The project board item titled "Impediment: The `scrum_update_story` tool is currently failing with a GraphQL error" (PVTI `PVTI_lAHOAmfLjc4BWiTtzgs66F4`) has its underlying GitHub issue link pointing to `MesseBuddy/issues/13` ("Story B: Backend Abstraction Layer (Phase 5)") — a different repository. A comment intended for the impediment was posted to `MesseBuddy/issues/13` instead, with no warning or error returned by the tool.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a project board item from repository A to a GitHub Projects board that also contains items from repository B
2. Ensure the board item's displayed title/content diverges from the linked GitHub issue in repo B
3. Call `scrum_update_story` with a `comment` on that board item's project item ID
4. Observe the comment appears on the unrelated issue in repo B, not on the expected item

## Affected MCP tool

- scrum_update_story

## Severity

Major – incorrect output, workaround exists

## Additional context

The root cause is that GitHub Projects v2 board items can be linked to issues from any repository in the organisation. The `scrum_update_story` comment path follows the linked GitHub issue node ID without validating that it belongs to the expected repository. The board item display title is stored separately on the project item and can differ from the linked issue's actual title, making the mismatch invisible to the caller.

**Workaround:** Verify the `url` field returned by `scrum_get_story` matches the expected repository before posting a comment.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scrum_update_story` detects when the linked GitHub issue belongs to a repository other than the primary project repository (from config) and warns the caller before posting
- [ ] The warning includes the linked issue's actual URL and title so the caller can make an informed decision
- [ ] Alternatively: the tool documentation clearly states that comments are posted to the linked GitHub issue, not to the project board item display, and `scrum_get_story` always surfaces the `url` prominently in its response

content.body:
## Problem statement

`FieldValueMutator` has two independent defects:

1. **Type inconsistency** — `gh` is typed `typeof graphql` (a bare function) and is called as `this.gh(query, vars)`. All other services use the object-wrapper form `this.gh.graphql(...)`. This is inconsistent and incompatible with `GitHubClient`.
2. **String interpolation in mutations** — All five field-setting mutations interpolate values directly into the GraphQL string instead of using named variables, creating an injection risk and losing type safety on responses.

`FieldValueMutator` was written before the `GitHubClient` interface existed. String interpolation was used as the path of least resistance during initial implementation.

- Inconsistent `gh` typing makes the codebase harder to reason about and blocks transport-layer improvements
- No typed generics on mutation responses means errors in the response shape go undetected at compile time

## Proposed approach

1. Update `gh` field to `GitHubClient`; replace all `this.gh(...)` bare calls with `this.gh.graphql(...)`
2. Parameterize all five mutation methods (`setFieldStatus`, `setFieldSprint`, `setFieldStoryPoints`, `setFieldPriority`, `setFieldAssignee`) with named GraphQL variables and typed response generics
3. Leave `clearField` paths unchanged — they already use parameterized variables

The use-case layer currently depends on the full `ProjectBackend` interface, which includes methods that are not required by every use case (e.g., file system operations). This violates the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP).

During initial development, a monolithic `ProjectBackend` was used for simplicity. As the project matured and specialized ports were introduced, the use cases were not updated to use these narrower interfaces.

- Violates ISP and makes the architecture more fragile.
- Makes it harder to swap out or mock specific parts of the backend for testing.

1. For each use case file in `src/scrum/`, identify the minimum set of methods required from the backend.

content.title: [Bug]: Backlog field data missing for all items; label mutations silently fail on Draft Issues
content.body:
## Expected behaviour

- `scrum_get_backlog` returns correct `status`, `story_points`, and `priority` values for all items — both Draft Issues and regular Issues.
- `scrum_update_story` with a `labels` update on a Draft Issue applies the labels transparently, auto-converting the Draft Issue to a full GitHub Issue when necessary.

## Actual behaviour

### Problem 1 — Backlog listing returns null for all board fields

Every item returned by `scrum_get_backlog` shows `status: null`, `story_points: null`, `priority: null`.

`StoryQueryService.getBacklogStories()` passes `sprintFieldIds` to `PaginatedProjectItemFetcher`, triggering a query optimisation in `pagination.ts` that only renders `ProjectV2ItemFieldIterationValue` sub-fields. All other field-value node types (`ProjectV2ItemFieldSingleSelectValue`, `ProjectV2ItemFieldNumberValue`) return as bare `{ __typename }` with no value fields. `extractBoardFields` finds nothing to extract.

### Problem 2 — Label and comment mutations throw on Draft Issues

`scrum_update_story` with `labels`, `scrum_update_story` with `assignees`, and `addComment` all throw `DRAFT_ISSUE_CONSTRAINT` on Draft Issues. Draft Issues have no backing GitHub Issue node, so any mutation that targets an Issue node ID fails.

## Steps to reproduce

**Problem 1:**
1. Call `scrum_get_backlog`
2. Observe `status: null`, `story_points: null`, `priority: null` on every returned item

**Problem 2:**
1. Identify a Draft Issue on the board
2. Call `scrum_update_story` with `labels: ["bug"]` on that item
3. Observe `DRAFT_ISSUE_CONSTRAINT` error

## Affected MCP tool

- scrum_get_backlog (Problem 1)
- scrum_update_story (Problem 2)

## Severity

Major – incorrect output, workaround exists

## Additional context

Discovered during Sprint 1 board health diagnostics (2026-05-15), follow-on to #32.

**Fix for Problem 1:** Remove `sprintFieldIds` from the backlog fetcher options. `isBacklogItem` still works correctly with the full field fragment since sprint iteration nodes remain present or absent regardless.

**Fix for Problem 2:** In `StoryMutationService`, before any operation requiring a backing Issue node, if `resolved.issueId === null`, call `convertProjectV2DraftIssueItemToIssue` with the item ID and repository node ID (available via `labelResolver.fetchRepoNodeId()`), then use the returned Issue ID for the mutation.

```graphql
mutation ConvertDraftIssue($itemId: ID!, $repositoryId: ID!) {
  convertProjectV2DraftIssueItemToIssue(input: {
    itemId: $itemId
    repositoryId: $repositoryId
  }) {
    item { id content { ... on Issue { id number } } }
  }
}
```

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Field data (Problem 1)
- [ ] `scrum_get_backlog` returns correct `status`, `story_points`, and `priority` values for regular Issues
- [ ] `scrum_get_backlog` returns correct `status`, `story_points`, and `priority` values for Draft Issues
- [ ] `isBacklogItem` still correctly filters out sprint-assigned items (no regression)
- [ ] `deno check src/index.ts` passes

### Draft Issue auto-conversion (Problem 2)
- [ ] Calling `scrum_update_story` with `labels` on a Draft Issue converts it to a full Issue transparently and applies the labels
- [ ] Calling `scrum_update_story` with `assignees` on a Draft Issue converts and assigns
- [ ] Calling `addComment` on a Draft Issue converts and posts the comment
- [ ] The conversion uses `convertProjectV2DraftIssueItemToIssue` — the project item ID is preserved; only the content type changes
- [ ] If conversion fails, a clear `GitHubApiError` is thrown with recovery guidance
- [ ] Draft Issues only having project-board fields set (`status`, `sprint`, `story_points`, `priority`) are **not** converted — those mutations work on the project item ID directly
- [ ] `deno check src/index.ts` passes

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Fix LabelResolver — DRY violation and hashToColor visibility
content.body:
## Problem statement

`LabelResolver` has two independent issues:

1. **DRY violation** — `resolveLabelNodeIds`, `resolveOrCreateLabel`, and `addLabel` each independently issue `GET_REPO_LABELS_QUERY`, making three separate network round-trips to fetch the same data.
2. **Visibility** — `hashToColor` is `public` despite being an internal utility used only within the class, creating an unintended dependency surface for callers.
3. **Type** — The `gh` field uses an ad-hoc type `{ graphql: typeof graphql }` instead of `GitHubClient`.

## Root cause

Each public method was written independently without extracting a shared fetch helper. `hashToColor` was given `public` visibility without considering encapsulation — likely left over from early development when it was tested directly.

## Affected architectural layer

GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Risk if deferred

- Every label operation issues redundant network calls, increasing latency and GitHub API rate-limit consumption
- Callers can depend on `hashToColor`, creating an unintended contract that makes the color algorithm harder to change

## Proposed approach

1. Extract `private async fetchAllLabels(): Promise<GitHubLabel[]>` to consolidate the query into a single call site
2. Replace all three `gh.graphql(GET_REPO_LABELS_QUERY, ...)` call sites with `await this.fetchAllLabels()`
3. Change `hashToColor` visibility to `private`
4. Update `gh` field type to `GitHubClient` (depends on #40)

## Done criteria

- [ ] `LabelResolver.gh` is typed `GitHubClient`
- [ ] `fetchAllLabels` is a single private method; `GET_REPO_LABELS_QUERY` appears exactly once in the class
- [ ] `hashToColor` is `private`
- [ ] All three public label methods (`resolveLabelNodeIds`, `resolveOrCreateLabel`, `addLabel`) pass `deno check`

content.title: [Bug]: Fix GraphQL injection vulnerability in resolveUserNodeId()
content.body:
## Expected behaviour

User input (`login`) is passed to the GitHub GraphQL API as a named variable, not interpolated into the query string. Special characters in usernames do not break the query, and attacker-controlled input cannot alter the query structure.

## Actual behaviour

`resolveUserNodeId()` interpolates `login` directly into the query string:

```graphql
query { user(login: "${login}") { id } }
```

A username containing `"` or other special characters breaks the query syntax. If attacker-controlled input reaches this function, the query structure can be altered.

**Location:** [`src/adapters/github/backend.ts:374`](src/adapters/github/backend.ts#L374)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Trigger any tool that resolves a user node ID (e.g. `scrum_update_story` with an `assignees` value, or `scrum_create_story` with assignees)
2. Supply a username containing a special character such as `user"name` or `user'name`
3. Observe a malformed GraphQL query error or unexpected query behaviour

## Affected MCP tool

- scrum_update_story
- scrum_create_story

## Severity

Major – incorrect output, workaround exists

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Refactor `resolveUserNodeId()` to use GraphQL variables instead of string interpolation
- [ ] Change query from `` `query { user(login: "${login}") { id } }` `` to `` `query GetUser($login: String!) { user(login: $login) { id } }` `` with variable injection
- [ ] Verify no regressions with `deno test`
- [ ] Test with special-character usernames: `user'o"b`, `user-name`, `user_name`
